events.summary: Noah Smith publishes an essay analyzing how rapid technological change, particularly artificial intelligence, has created unprecedented uncertainty about the future. The piece examines how Americans' optimism declined from 69% in 2016 to 59% in 2026, attributing this shift to the collapse of extrapolative expectations—the assumption that recent positive trends would continue indefinitely. Smith argues that the 1990s represented a peak in American optimism based on sustained economic growth, falling crime, Cold War victory, and global democratic expansion, but that subsequent shocks (9/11, financial crisis, Trump era) and current disruptions (AI, geopolitical instability, China's rise) have made the future unpredictable.
events.why_relevant: The essay documents a measurable decline in American confidence in the future and institutional predictability, reflecting broader erosion of shared expectations about democratic governance and social stability.
events.basis: The sudden rise of artificial intelligence has cast a great fog over our future... The political chaos of the last decade, and especially the governing style of the second Trump administration, has swept away much of what we thought we knew about American society.

events.title: DEA temporarily schedules bromazolam in Schedule I of Controlled Substances Act
events.summary: The Drug Enforcement Administration issued a temporary order placing bromazolam (8-bromo-1-methyl-6-phenyl-4H-benzo[f][1,2,4]triazolo[4,3-a][1,4]diazepine), a novel designer benzodiazepine, in Schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act effective immediately. events.title: EPA Finalizes Amendments to National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Polyether Polyols Production
events.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency finalized amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants (NESHAP) for the Polyether Polyols (PEPO) Production source category under Clean Air Act section 112. The EPA finalized ethylene oxide (EtO)-specific standards under section 112(d)(6) technology review authority rather than under the proposed section 112(f)(2) residual risk review. The rule establishes maximum achievable control technology (MACT) standards for process vents, storage vessels, equipment leaks, heat exchange systems, and wastewater in EtO service; revises standards for batch process vents and equipment leaks in organic HAP service; and finalizes operational and monitoring requirements for flares, work practice standards for maintenance activities, and electronic reporting requirements. The effective date is March 18, 2026, with compliance required by March 18, 2029 for existing sources.
